messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content:
The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the object and the damping coefficient.
Coefficient of damping is determined by the viscosity of the surrounding medium and the shape of the body.
Body geometry and fluid properties together define the magnitude of the resistive force.
Force is significant enough to be taken into account when the pendulum oscillates in a viscous medium such as air or water.
Water or any fluid with non-negligible viscosity requires the inclusion of this term in the pendulum equation.
Equation of motion for a damped physical pendulum must include the viscous term when energy dissipation affects the period or amplitude noticeably.
Noticeably, in most laboratory settings with a pendulum swinging in air, the damping is small but still measurable over time.
